4235.t: From εὐάγγελος (euángelos, “bringing good news”), from εὐ- (eu-, “good”) + ἀγγέλλω (angéllō, “to deliver”).

4284.t: From Proto-Hellenic *klāwī́ds, from Proto-Indo-European *kleh₂u- (“nail; pin; hook”, instruments, of old use for locking doors). Cognate with Latin clāvus (“nail; pin”), Old Church Slavonic ключь (ključĭ, “key”).

4248.t: Of unclear origin. Generally connected with ζύμη (zúmē, “leaven, beer yeast”), but the ablaut required (ō(u) : ū) is improbable.

4228.t: From Proto-Hellenic *dómos, from Proto-Indo-European *dṓm. Cognates include Latin domus, Sanskrit दम (dáma), Russian дом (dom), and Old Armenian տուն (tun).

4295.t: Unclear. Usually derived from κρότος (krótos, “beating”), as "beating of the veins in the temples", while Furnée instead connects it with κόρση (kórsē, “temple”), as well as, more distantly, κρόσσαι (króssai, “steps of pyramid”).

4212.t: From διαστέλλω (diastéllō) + -η (-ē, abstract noun suffix), from διά (diá, “apart”) + στέλλω (stéllō, “send”).

4243.t: From εὐχάριστος (eukhắrĭstos, “thankful, grateful”) + -ία (-ĭ́ā), from εὐ- (eu-, “good”) + χάρις (khắrĭs, “grace”) + -τος (-tos).

4287.t: Traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *kelh₂- (“to beat, break”), whence also Latin percellō (“to beat down, overturn”), but due to phonetic difficulties, Beekes prefers to take the verb as Pre-Greek.

4255.t: Related to θαλυκρός (thălŭkrós, “warm; glowing”), from Proto-Hellenic *tʰal-ukʷ-, likely of Pre-Greek origin. The connection with θάλλω (thắllō, “to make green”) is unlikely.

4223.t: Uncertain. Beekes mentions a connection with Lithuanian darýti (“to make; to do”).

4273.t: From κατα- (kătă-, “downwards, down”) + ῥέω (rhéō, “to flow, run, stream, gush”).

4220.t: By surface analysis, δίς (dĭ́s, “twice”) + -πλόος (-plóos, “-fold”). Compare ἁπλόος (hăplóos, “simple”), as well as Latin duplus (“double”), Proto-Germanic *twīflaz (“doubt”).

4203.t: According to Beekes, of Semitic origin, related to dalet. (A connection to delta, ultimately from the same Semitic source, has also been proposed.)

4256.t: Due to the improbability of the other explanations, Beekes suggests a Pre-Greek origin.

4288.t: From κλέπτω (kléptō, “to steal”) and the suffix -μα (-ma).

4261.t: Equivalent to κακο- (kako-, bad) + -ουργός (-ourgós, worker; maker).

4232.t: Possibly from a Proto-Indo-European *weyk- (“to become equal”), although there are no cognates outside of Greek. Cognate with εἰκών (eikṓn), ἔοικα (éoikă).

4204.t: From the aorist stem of δάπτω (dáptō, “to devour, consume”), with a suffix in -ιλ-.
